holidays.name: Electronic Greetings Day
holidays.description: A day to ditch the paper card and send a digital greeting instead. Think e-cards, texts, GIFs, and emoji-laden messages to friends, family, and that coworker you only talk to on Slack.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that emerged in the internet era as e-cards and email greetings grew popular, promoted by holiday-listing sites as a nod to digital communication.
holidays.funFact: The first commercial e-card sites appeared in the mid-1990s, and by the early 2000s millions of e-cards were being sent every year, especially around the holidays.

holidays.name: Square Dance Day
holidays.description: A day to grab a partner, put on your boots, and do-si-do. Callers shout instructions, dancers swing and promenade, and everybody tries not to get lost in the square.
holidays.origin: An informal observance celebrating American square dancing, a folk tradition with roots in English, Scottish, and French country dances brought over by settlers and later shaped by Western American culture.
holidays.funFact: Square dancing is the official state dance of more than 30 US states, which makes it one of the most widely recognized state symbols in the country.

holidays.name: Lemon Creme Pie Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the tangy, creamy, and dreamy dessert that combines tart citrus with a silky, cloud-like filling. Perfect for anyone who wants their dessert to be both puckery and comforting.
holidays.origin: A food observance created by dessert fans and promoted through food-holiday calendars, falling right after Thanksgiving when leftover pie energy is still running high.
holidays.funFact: Lemon pies became popular in the US partly because lemons were available year-round, unlike many seasonal fruits, and lemon meringue was a staple of mid-century diners.

holidays.name: Chaos Never Dies Day
holidays.description: A day to embrace the unpredictable, the messy, and the delightfully disorganized. Fans of anarchic humor and beloved chaotic characters celebrate by letting the day go off the rails a little.
holidays.origin: A lighthearted pop culture and internet-flavored observance that lets people lean into the post-holiday-weekend disorder and the general unpredictability of life.
holidays.funFact: Chaos theory, which studies how tiny changes can lead to huge outcomes, gave us the famous 'butterfly effect' idea popularized by meteorologist Edward Lorenz in the 1960s.

holidays.name: International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People
holidays.description: A United Nations observance dedicated to raising awareness and promoting dialogue on the Palestinian question, marked with meetings, statements, and exhibitions.
holidays.origin: Established by the UN General Assembly in 1977, it was set for November 29 to mark the date in 1947 when the Assembly adopted the partition plan for Palestine.
holidays.funFact: It is one of the UN's long-running annual observances, and it is often marked with special sessions held at UN headquarters and offices around the world.
